args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the latest deploy. Service status reported unhealthy=true with an error rate of 0.18. Deployment history shows v2.3.1 as unhealthy in production; the most recent production-healthy release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and also unhealthy). Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The first rollback attempt partially failed mid-rollout (orchestrator error, halted after us-east, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 and us-west/eu-west on v2.3.1); a retry completed the rollout to v2.3.0 in all three regions. Post-rollback verification shows healthy=true and error rate down to 0.002. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is not yet identified and requires investigation before re-deploying.

trace.final:
The incident was in fact created (INC-0001) despite the timeout response, so I did not retry and risk a duplicate.

## Summary

**Rollback completed and service recovered.**

- **Diagnosis:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), `healthy=false` with 0.31%... specifically error rate 0.13→0.18 range — reported 0.18 at the time. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 as `unhealthy`; v2.3.0 was the most recent production-healthy release (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was correctly skipped).
- **Rollback:** First attempt returned a partial failure ("rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"), leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). I re-checked status, then retried the rollback, which completed: all three regions now on v2.3.0.
- **Verification:** `healthy=true`, error rate down to 0.002 across all regions.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 opened, SEV2, documenting the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure/retry), and the verified recovery. The create call timed out client-side but the incident was recorded; I confirmed via list rather than re-filing.

Two things worth flagging:
1. Release v2.3.0 is a previously-healthy production version, so no change-manager approval was required for this rollback.
2. The root cause of the v2.3.1 failure is still unknown — it should be diagnosed before any re-deploy attempt. Also, the orchestrator error on the first rollback attempt may indicate a separate platform issue worth investigating. If you want to retry v2.3.1 later, note that deploying a version that has never been healthy in production would require change-manager approval.
